summary: Source decomposition of the arithmetic Galois-representation API, from six primary sources: Deligne's Antwerp paper for Grothendieck's monodromy theorem and the definition of a Weil-Deligne representation with its dependence on a chosen geometric Frobenius; Serre's Duke paper for the Artin conductor with its wild part and for tame inertia and the level of a character; Khare-Wintenberger and Dieulefait-Pacetti for Dickson's classification, its characteristic-2 refinement, the bad-dihedral definition and the niveau analysis; Allen-Calegari-Caraiani-Gee-Helm-Le Hung-Newton-Scholze-Taylor-Thorne for the enormity condition and its coefficient-extension invariance, which this reading confirms verbatim against the atlas stage text; Chenevier and Deligne-Serre for recognition by characteristic polynomials and coefficient descent; and Faltings for Tate modules, semisimplicity and the isogeny criterion. One boundary is recorded sharply: the displayed identity defining a Weil-Deligne representation did not survive text extraction, so the arithmetic-versus-geometric Frobenius normalisation that the stage text asserts is NOT established by this reading.

nodes.title: Grothendieck's monodromy theorem and the passage from a lambda-adic representation to a Weil-Deligne representation
nodes.statement: Let (V, rho) be a lambda-adic representation of W(Kbar/K) for K a local field with residue field of cardinality q and lambda of residue characteristic different from that of K. Grothendieck's theorem (the source's 8.2, attributed there and proved in its reference [13]): there exists a nilpotent N in End(V)(-1) such that for sigma in a subgroup of FINITE INDEX of the inertia group I one has the displayed formula rho(sigma) = exp(t_lambda(sigma) N); this N is unique, hence Galois-invariant, and for w in W(Kbar/K) it satisfies rho(w) N rho(w)^{-1} = q^{v(w)} N. Definition 8.4.1: for E a field of characteristic 0, a representation of 'W(Kbar/K) over E is a pair (rho', N) consisting of a finite-dimensional representation rho': W(Kbar/K) -> GL(V) over E and a nilpotent endomorphism N of V satisfying the displayed relation (8.4.1.1). Construction 8.4.2 attaches such a pair to a lambda-adic (V, rho) after CHOOSING a geometric Frobenius F in W(Kbar/K) and an isomorphism T: Z_l(1) -> Z_l; Lemme 8.4.3 shows the isomorphism class of (rho', N) depends only on rho and not on the choices of F and T.
hypotheses: lambda must have residue characteristic different from that of K; this is the l different from p hypothesis of the stage
the nilpotent N lies in End(V)(-1), i.e. it is Tate-twisted; forgetting the twist is what makes the conjugation relation's exponent convention ambiguous
quasi-unipotence is only on a subgroup of FINITE INDEX of inertia; rho itself need not be unipotent on all of I
the construction 8.4.2 depends on choosing a GEOMETRIC Frobenius F and a trivialization T of Z_l(1); Lemme 8.4.3 removes the dependence only up to isomorphism
the source's proof of Lemme 8.4.3 works by changing F to F rho and T to sT and showing (rho', N) is isomorphic to (rho', aN) for every a in E^*
proofSteps: The source states 8.2 as Grothendieck's theorem and refers to its [13] for the proof, which was NOT read here.

It then gives two descriptions of lambda-adic representations independent of the topology of E_lambda: 8.3 (more intrinsic, through an algebraic group) and 8.4 (more elementary), remarking that 8.4 suffices for its purposes.
8.4.2 produces (rho', N) from (V, rho), and Lemme 8.4.3 proves independence of the choices.

Check that the Frobenius semisimplification, the semisimplification and the full object are three different things by exhibiting a representation where they differ

nodes.title: Tame inertia, the level of a character, and the fundamental characters of levels one and two
nodes.statement: Let G_p = Gal(Qbar_p/Q_p), I its inertia subgroup, I_p the wild inertia (the largest pro-p subgroup of I), and I_t = I/I_p the tame quotient, which is identified with the inverse limit of the F_{p^n}^*. A character of I_t is said to be of level n if it factors through F_{p^n}^* and through no F_{p^m}^* for m a proper divisor of n. The two fundamental characters psi, psi' of level 2 are the characters I_t -> F_{p^2}^* -> F_p-bar^* corresponding to the two embeddings of F_{p^2} into F_p-bar; the fundamental character of level 1 is the mod p cyclotomic character chi, and psi psi' = chi. For a 2-dimensional continuous rho_p: G_p -> GL(V) over F_p-bar, I_p acts trivially on the semisimplification V^{ss}, so I_t acts diagonalizably on V^{ss} through two characters phi, phi'; these are of level 1 or of level 2, and in the level-2 case phi' = phi^p and phi = phi'^p. A separate source fixes notation for the lifts: omega_p denotes the Teichmuller lift of the mod p cyclotomic character, and omega_{p,2} a fundamental character of level 2 valued in F_{p^2}^*, with the same symbol used for its Teichmuller lift and for all its l-adic incarnations.
hypotheses: the identification of I_t with the inverse limit of the F_{p^n}^* and the triviality of I_p on a semisimple F_p-bar-representation are both quoted from an external source in the text read
'level' is a property of a character of I_t, not of a representation of G_p
the dichotomy level 1 versus level 2 is specific to dimension 2; the argument uses that conjugation by a Frobenius lift acts on I_t by u -> u^p and hence permutes {phi, phi'}
the Teichmuller lifts and their l-adic incarnations for arbitrary l are denoted by the same symbols in the second source; the ambiguity is deliberate and must be tracked
proofSteps: The dichotomy and its proof are the source's Proposition 1: with s lifting Frobenius, s u s^{-1} = u^p mod I_p for u in I, so the pair {phi, phi'} is stable under p-th power; either both are fixed (level 1) or they are swapped (level 2).
In the level-2 case V is irreducible, since a stable line would give a character of I_t extendable to G_p, hence of level 1.
acceptance: Check that the product of the two level-2 fundamental characters is the mod p cyclotomic character
Check on an explicit supersingular elliptic curve that the tame characters are the two level-2 fundamental characters

nodes.title: The Artin conductor exponent, its wild part, and the prime-to-p conductor N(rho-bar)
nodes.statement: Let l be a prime different from p and choose an extension of the l-adic valuation to Qbar; let G_0 superset G_1 superset ... be the corresponding ramification groups of the finite image G of rho, and V^i the subspace fixed by G_i. Define n(l, rho) = sum over i >= 0 of (1/[G_0 : G_i]) dim(V/V^i). Equivalently n(l, rho) = dim V/V^{G_0} + b(V), where b(V) is the 'wild invariant' of the G_0-module V. Consequences: (a) n(l, rho) is a nonnegative integer; (b) n(l, rho) = 0 if and only if G_0 = 1, i.e. rho is unramified at l; (c) n(l, rho) = dim V/V^{G_0} if and only if G_1 = 1, i.e. rho is tamely ramified at l. The prime-to-p conductor is N = product over l different from p of l^{n(l, rho)}; it is prime to p by construction.
hypotheses: the definition uses the ramification filtration in LOWER numbering of the finite quotient through which rho factors at l, and the sum is over i >= 0 including the wild part
integrality of n(l, rho) is a theorem (it is the content of (a)), not evident from the formula
the definition is the characteristic-zero one, applied to a residual representation; the source says so explicitly and restricts the product to places prime to p
the equivalence n(l, rho) = dim V/V^{G_0} characterises tameness; the wild term b(V) is not omitted at l = 2 or 3
proofSteps: The source defines n(l, rho) by the displayed sum (1.2.1), rewrites it as (1.2.2) with the wild invariant b(V) citing an external reference, and then reads off (a), (b), (c).
The product (1.2.3) over l different from p defines N.
acceptance: Check integrality of n(l, rho) on a wildly ramified example at l = 2
Check that reduction of an l-adic representation does not increase n(l, -) at l different from p, which the stage requires but which is not proved in the source read here

nodes.title: The classification of finite irreducible subgroups of GL_2, its p = 2 refinement, and the dihedral consequences
nodes.statement: Dickson: for any prime p, a finite subgroup of GL_2(F_p-bar) acting irreducibly on the plane has projective image isomorphic to a dihedral group, A_4, S_4, A_5, PSL_2(F_0) or PGL_2(F_0) for F_0 a finite subfield of F_p-bar; PSL_2(F_0) is simple nonabelian as soon as |F_0| >= 4. Refinement at p = 2: a finite SOLVABLE subgroup of GL_2(F_2-bar) acting irreducibly has DIHEDRAL projective image; S_4 is excluded because an element of GL_2(F_2-bar) of 2-power order has order 1 or 2, and A_4 is excluded because its normal subgroup of order 4 would force the group into the upper triangular matrices, contradicting irreducibility. A second source records the same statement with the additional gloss that the A_4 case 'corresponds to a Borel subgroup over F_4'. Consequence used repeatedly: if a residual representation has a projective image of order divisible by a prime t > 5 and is solvable, then the projective image is dihedral.
hypotheses: the refinement is over F_2-bar and uses characteristic 2 twice; it fails over F_p-bar for odd p
Dickson's classification is quoted from an external reference and not proved in either source read
the simplicity of PSL_2(F_0) requires |F_0| >= 4
proofSteps: The dyadic refinement is proved in the source in four lines, as recorded in the statement.
Both sources then use it to reduce the solvable dyadic case of Serre's conjecture to the dihedral case, which is handled by Rohrlich-Tunnell.
acceptance: Check the exclusion of A_4 by exhibiting the normal subgroup of order 4 inside a Sylow 2-subgroup of GL_2(F_2-bar) and verifying it is unipotent

nodes.title: Bad dihedral representations, the equivalence of the two irreducibility hypotheses, and the weights they force
nodes.statement: Definition: a residual representation rho-bar: Gal_Q -> GL_2(F_p-bar) which is irreducible but becomes reducible on restriction to Gal_{Q(sqrt(p*))}, where p* = (-1)^{(p-1)/2} p, is called BAD DIHEDRAL. Lemma: for p odd and rho-bar odd and continuous, rho-bar restricted to Gal_{Q(sqrt(p*))} is irreducible if and only if rho-bar restricted to Gal_{Q(zeta_p)} is irreducible - so Wiles's condition and the Q(zeta_p) condition used in the lifting theorems agree. Lemma (weights of a bad dihedral representation): for p odd and rho-bar odd, continuous and bad dihedral, either p = 2 k(rho-bar) - 3 (the niveau-2 case) or p = 2 k(rho-bar) - 1 (the niveau-1 case), assuming as usual that after twisting all Serre weights lie in [2, p+1]. Remark: over Q a representation with Serre level 1 cannot be bad dihedral in the niveau-2 case, so at level 1 only p = 2k(rho-bar)-1 occurs, and then k(rho-bar) is even, so a bad dihedral representation of Serre level 1 can only occur when p is congruent to 3 mod 4. Separately: for p different from 2 and det rho = chi, irreducibility over F_p implies ABSOLUTE irreducibility, because det rho odd makes the eigenvalues of rho(c) equal to +1 and -1, which are distinct when p is odd, so any decomposition over F_p-bar would be the eigenvector decomposition of rho(c) and hence rational over F_p.
hypotheses: the definition of bad dihedral uses the specific quadratic field Q(sqrt(p*)), the unique quadratic extension of Q unramified outside p
the weight lemma assumes the normalisation 2 <= k(rho-bar) <= p+1, obtained after twisting
the niveau-2 exclusion at level 1 is attributed to a lemma of Wintenberger in the level-one paper, an external input not read here
the oddness-to-absolute-irreducibility argument needs p different from 2; at p = 2 the eigenvalues of rho(c) coincide
proofSteps: The equivalence lemma argues that reducibility over Q(zeta_p) forces solvable image, and then eliminates the Borel and exceptional cases.

The weight lemma follows the lines of an argument of Ribet: irreducible image with dihedral projective image and p >= 3 imply no elements of order p in the image, so all matrices are semisimple and the image of I_p is cyclic; in the niveau-2 case the inertia image is psi^{k-1} + psi'^{k-1}, whose projective order is the order of psi^{(k-1)(p-1)}, the (k-1)-st power of a character of order p+1, which has order at most 2 exactly when (p+1)/2 divides k-1, and k <= p then forces p = 2k-3.
The second source records that the earlier statement of this lemma (in the Serre-conjecture paper) 'lacks some details' and that this is why the replacement proof is given.
acceptance: Check both niveau cases on explicit representations, confirming p = 2k-3 and p = 2k-1 respectively
Check that at p = 2 the oddness argument fails by exhibiting an F_2-irreducible representation that becomes reducible over F_4

nodes.title: Chebotarev recognition, realizability over the field of characteristic polynomials, and the determinant formalism
nodes.statement: Recognition: two continuous SEMISIMPLE representations of G_Q with the same characteristic polynomials of Frobenius on a set of primes of density 1 are isomorphic, by Cebotarev together with the fact that a semisimple representation over a field is determined by its characteristic polynomials. Coefficient descent: if phi: Phi -> GL_n(k') is a semisimple representation over a FINITE field k' and k is a subfield containing the coefficients of det(1 - phi(s)T) for all s, then phi is realizable over k; the proof uses that the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial, so there is no Schur index, and that phi and its Galois conjugates have the same characteristic polynomials and are semisimple, hence isomorphic. Determinant formalism: the passage from a system of characteristic polynomials to an actual representation is by Chenevier's determinants, which work over an arbitrary base ring; Theorem A recovers a unique semisimple representation over an algebraically closed field from a determinant, and Theorem B produces a genuine representation over a henselian local ring with algebraically closed residue field when the residual representation is irreducible. The determinant formalism, not pseudocharacters, is needed when the residue characteristic is small: the source records a gap in Rouquier's Lemma 4.1 (and hence Theorem 4.2) where d! is required to be invertible.
hypotheses: recognition requires SEMISIMPLE representations; without semisimplification the characteristic polynomials do not determine the isomorphism class
in small residual characteristic traces alone are insufficient: the descent statement is about the coefficients of the characteristic polynomials, not traces
the descent statement requires k' FINITE; over an infinite field the Brauer group need not vanish and a Schur index can obstruct
Chenevier Theorem B requires an algebraically closed residue field, which a localized Hecke algebra does not have; the bridge is not supplied by the sources read
proofSteps: Cebotarev gives density-1 Frobenius classes; semisimplicity plus equality of characteristic polynomials gives isomorphism, by the theorem cited as Curtis-Reiner 30.16.
The finite-field descent is the source's Lemme 6.13.
Chenevier's Theorems A and B supply the general determinant-to-representation machinery.

nodes.title: Tate modules of abelian varieties: semisimplicity, the Tate conjecture, and the isogeny criterion
nodes.statement: Let K be a finite extension of Q, A an abelian variety over K, pi = Gal(Kbar/K), l a prime, T_l(A) = inverse limit of A[l^n](Kbar). Then: (a) the representation of pi on T_l(A) tensor Q_l is SEMISIMPLE (Satz 3); (b) the map End_K(A) tensor Z_l -> End_pi(T_l(A)) is an isomorphism (Satz 4); (c) for a finite set S of places of K and d > 0, there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of d-fold polarized abelian varieties over K with good reduction outside S (Satz 6, the Shafarevich conjecture). Korollar 1: Hom_K(A_1, A_2) tensor Z_l -> Hom_pi(T_l(A_1), T_l(A_2)) is an isomorphism. Korollar 2: for abelian varieties A_1, A_2 over K the following are equivalent: (i) A_1 and A_2 are isogenous; (ii) T_l(A_1) tensor Q_l and T_l(A_2) tensor Q_l are isomorphic as pi-modules; (iii) L_v(s, A_1) = L_v(s, A_2) for almost all places v; (iv) for all v. The L-series is defined as the product over almost all places of 1/det(1 - (Nv)^{-s} F_v | T_l(A)), and the local L-factors are independent of l. Korollar 3: for A over K and d > 0 there are only finitely many isomorphism classes of d-fold polarized B over K with T_l(A) isomorphic to T_l(B) for all l.
hypotheses: K must be a NUMBER FIELD; the source's whole method is the transfer of Zarhin's function-field arguments to the number-field case through Arakelov theory
the equivalence (ii) iff (iii) uses Satz 3 (semisimplicity) together with Cebotarev; without semisimplicity the local factors do not determine the module
Korollar 3's proof needs, after enlarging K: semistable reduction for all the B, principal polarization, and a uniform bound N on the largest l-power in the degree of an isogeny A -> B
the local L-factors' independence of l is asserted as known ('bekanntlich') in the passage read, for the places where the product is taken
proofSteps: The source proves Shafarevich first for isogeny classes, using heights of abelian varieties and the finiteness Satz 1 for pairs with bounded height.
Korollar 1 is Satz 4 applied to A_1 x A_2; Korollar 2 assembles Satz 3 and Satz 4 with Cebotarev; Korollar 3 uses a height bound extracted from the remark after Lemma 5 and then Satz 1.
acceptance: Check the Weil pairing determinant det T_l(E) = chi_l for an elliptic curve, and oddness over Q
Check the good-reduction Frobenius polynomial 1 - a_v T + (Nv) T^2 against the local L-factor used in Korollar 2

nodes.title: The 'enormous' condition for Taylor-Wiles data, its failure when p divides n, and its invariance under coefficient extension
nodes.statement: Let k be an algebraic extension of F_p and ad^0 the space of trace-zero matrices in M_{n x n}(k) with the adjoint GL_n(k)-action. An ABSOLUTELY IRREDUCIBLE subgroup H of GL_n(k) is called enormous over k if: (1) H has no nontrivial quotient of p-power order; (2) H^0(H, ad^0) = H^1(H, ad^0) = 0; (3) for any simple k[H]-submodule W of ad^0 there is a REGULAR SEMISIMPLE h in H with W^h nonzero. The condition depends only on the image of H in PGL_n(k). If p divides n then NO subgroup of GL_n(k) is enormous, because ad^0 then contains the scalar matrices. Lemma 6.2.30: for an algebraic extension k'/k and H contained in GL_n(k), H is enormous over k if and only if it is enormous over k'. The definition is essentially equivalent to the one in the literature cited as [KT17, Def. 4.10] provided k is large enough to contain all eigenvalues of the elements of H.
hypotheses: H must be absolutely irreducible as part of the definition, not merely irreducible
condition (3) requires h to be REGULAR SEMISIMPLE; dropping regularity changes the condition
the condition is vacuous - unsatisfiable - when p divides n; the source says so explicitly
the equivalence with [KT17, Def. 4.10] holds only under the extra hypothesis that k contains all eigenvalues of elements of H
in the applications the group is the image of rho restricted to G_{F(zeta_p)}, not the image of rho itself
proofSteps: Lemma 6.2.30's proof: only condition (3) needs attention, and it is equivalent to the statement that for ALL nonzero k[H]-submodules W of ad^0 there is a regular semisimple h with W^h nonzero. In that form enormity over k' clearly implies enormity over k.

Conversely, the property V^h = 0 is closed under direct sums and quotients (because V^h is nonzero if and only if V_h is nonzero). For V inside ad^0 tensor k', sigma h v = h sigma v for sigma in Gal(k'/k) since H is inside GL_n(k), so V^h is nonzero if and only if (sigma V)^h is nonzero. Hence if W' is a simple k'[H]-submodule with no h-invariants, the same holds for all sigma W' and for the submodule generated by their sum; that submodule is stable under H and Gal(k'/k), so by descent it has the form W tensor k'. Applying condition (3) to a k[H]-simple submodule of W gives W^h nonzero for some regular semisimple h, and hence the same for W'.
acceptance: Check that for n = p no subgroup is enormous, by exhibiting the scalars inside ad^0
Check condition (2) for an explicit H = SL_2(F_p) with p >= 5 and confirm it fails for small p

nodes.title: Continuity, descent of the coefficient field, and lattice independence of the residual semisimplification
nodes.statement: For a continuous representation rho: G -> GL_n(K_lambda) with G compact and K_lambda a local field, compactness of rho(G) gives a stable lattice, so rho may be conjugated into GL_n(O_lambda); reduction modulo the maximal ideal then gives a residual representation whose SEMISIMPLIFICATION is independent of the chosen lattice, by the Brauer-Nesbitt theorem in characteristic p. A continuous representation into GL_n(F_p-bar) with the discrete topology has finite image and hence descends to a finite coefficient field. Two uses of these facts in the sources read: the passage from rho_lambda over K_lambda to rho-bar over the residue field proceeds exactly this way - 'quitte a remplacer rho_lambda par une representation isomorphe, on peut supposer que rho_lambda(G) est contenu dans GL_2(O-hat_lambda)' - and the resulting semisimple residual representation is then descended to the field generated by the coefficients of its characteristic polynomials.
hypotheses: compactness of the image is what produces the lattice; without it there need be no stable lattice
independence of the lattice holds only after semisimplification; the reduction itself depends on the lattice
the descent to a finite field uses that the target is discrete, so continuity forces finite image
the Brauer-Nesbitt theorem in characteristic p is used but was NOT read in a source in this pass
proofSteps: The source conjugates rho_lambda into GL_2 of the ring of integers of the completion, reduces mod lambda, and takes the semisimplification.

It then observes via Cebotarev that every element of the image is a Frobenius, so the characteristic polynomials have coefficients in the field k_f generated by the eigenvalues, and applies the descent lemma.
acceptance: Check that two non-isomorphic lattices can give non-isomorphic reductions with isomorphic semisimplifications
Check that a continuous representation into GL_2(F_p-bar) with the discrete topology has finite image

The stage requires the conductor of an l-adic representation to include the MONODROMY term, i.e. the contribution dim V^{I} - dim (Ker N)^{I}.
